items.title: Daniel Ricciardo: Max Verstappen will "go down as one of the best ever"
items.summary: Daniel Ricciardo says Max Verstappen will "go down as one of the best ever", and admits he cannot comprehend what Red Bull has achieved in its first season building its own power units. Ricciardo was Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull from 2016 until the end of 2018, and is now an ambassador for Ford, whose partnership with Red Bull Powertrains made its race debut this season.

items.title: Oscar Piastri reveals unexpected upside of being out of F1 title fight
items.summary: Oscar Piastri says he misses the pressure of fighting for the Formula 1 world championship. The McLaren driver led the standings for much of last year and was in a season-long battle against his team-mate Lando Norris for the title.

items.title: Lando Norris questions Charles Leclerc's Brazilian GP penalty: "Just racing"
items.summary: McLaren Formula 1 driver Lando Norris has questioned Charles Leclerc's penalty after the Brazilian Grand Prix, which cost the Ferrari driver seventh place. Leclerc tapped the left rear of Liam Lawson's Racing Bulls car at Turn 12 on the penultimate lap of the race at Interlagos.

items.title: Max Verstappen names the one condition that would make him retire from F1
items.summary: Max Verstappen says he would walk away from Formula 1 if he ever stopped believing he was the best driver in the field. The four-time world champion has not won the title since 2024, with Lando Norris taking the championship win last year and Kimi Antonelli wrapping up the 2026 championship in Mexico earlier this month.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton tours Gaza aid operation at Egypt's Rafah border
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has been to see the aid operation at Egypt's border with Gaza, two days after racing at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. The seven-time world champion arrived in El Arish, in Egypt's North Sinai region, on Tuesday, and was met at the airport by the region's governor, Khaled Megawer.

items.title: ‘Kimi Antonelli isn’t Ayrton Senna yet, but he may be a Senninha’ – Toto Wolff
items.summary: To this day, Ayrton Senna remains the last Brazilian Formula 1 driver to have won the world championship. But as a new generation of Auriverde racers finally emerges, they’re not the ones drawing comparisons to the country’s legend.

items.title: FIA reveals latest ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
items.summary: The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers.

items.title: Honda struggling to explain Lance Stroll’s 13th DNF of the season
items.summary: Honda says it needs to find the root cause of Lance Stroll’s multiple battery issues after yet another retirement for the Aston Martin Formula 1 driver in the Brazilian Grand Prix. Stroll’s race in Sao Paulo ended after 30 laps, as he lay 18th, 28 seconds adrift of 12-placed team-mate Fernando Alonso.

items.title: Laurent Mekies: Liam Lawson’s fate has nothing to do with me
items.summary: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies says it’s up to Racing Bulls whether to retain Liam Lawson or promote Nikola Tsolov to a race seat in the 2027 Formula 1 season. Rookie Arvid Lindblad is set to get a second campaign in the world championship next year, but the identity of his team-mate has been uncertain.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix announces pre-race music line-up
items.summary: American DJ Steve Aoki will return to the Las Vegas Grand Prix grid this year for a performance before the race on 21 November. He will be joined by fellow DJ MORTEN and singer Jordin Sparks as part of the pre-race line-up.

items.title: George Russell "keeps getting kicked" as F1 pundit addresses 2026 struggles
items.summary: Former IndyCar Series driver and F1 TV pundit James Hinchcliffe believes George Russell had good reason to look "a bit defeated" after another difficult afternoon at the Brazilian Grand Prix. While Mercedes ended the weekend on a high, securing the constructors' championship, Russell endured another frustrating race.

items.title: George Russell teases imminent karting announcement as F1 fans spot major clue
items.summary: George Russell has teased an imminent announcement linked to karting on 12 November. The Mercedes driver posted a video to Instagram on Monday with the caption "Stay tuned". He talks about his first steps in motorsport over footage of himself racing karts as a boy, including a kart carrying the number 63 that he still uses in Formula 1.

items.title: Apple TV confirms free F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix coverage: How to watch in the US
items.summary: Formula 1 fans in the United States will be able to watch the Las Vegas Grand Prix for free after Apple TV confirmed the whole race weekend will be available to stream with no subscription needed. The free coverage will include every on-track session from first practice on Thursday evening through to qualifying and Saturday night's grand prix.

items.title: What's behind Oscar Piastri's split with Mark Webber – and what it means for his F1 career
items.summary: On the Monday after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber announced in a joint statement that the latter and Ann Neal would no longer manage the 25-year-old McLaren driver. The timing may come as a surprise – now rather than at the end of the season – but the news itself had been on the cards for some time.

items.title: Why Mercedes says a repeat of its 2014-2021 dominance is "impossible"
items.summary: Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin has argued that the Brackley outfit cannot expect to repeat its run of eight consecutive constructors' titles after its 2026 success. Mercedes clinched its ninth constructors' championship at Interlagos on Sunday, ending a wait that began after the last of those eight in 2021.

items.title: George Russell has lost 90 points to Max Verstappen in F1 2026 runner-up battle
items.summary: Mercedes is considering giving George Russell “all the force” to secure a 1-2 in the drivers’ championship after a nightmare run of form.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton sends message to Ferrari fans after 'devastating' Brazil GP
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has told fans he is "devastated" by the outcome of his Brazilian Grand Prix, which began with an impressive charge from the back of the grid and finished with a spin in the closing laps. The Ferrari driver shared his thoughts on Instagram on Monday after finishing ninth at Interlagos on Sunday.

items.title: Ayrton Senna's rare Honda NSX smashes auction estimate with record six-figure sale
items.summary: A Honda NSX used by three-time Formula 1 champion Ayrton Senna has set an auction record for the model. The car, which had been estimated to sell for between £500,000 and £800,000 prior to the auction, sold for £871,250 at RM Sotheby's in London on 31 October.

items.title: How Max Verstappen beat Red Bull's own simulation tools with P2 in Brazil
items.summary: For the third year in a row, Verstappen produced an impressive comeback drive in the Formula 1 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. While the Dutchman won from 17th on the grid in 2024 and climbed from the pitlane to third place last year, this time he charged from 21st to second.

items.title: Who slept best last night: Toto Wolff
items.summary: Toto Wolff didn't need to brag when, on Sunday evening in Sao Paulo, he was asked about his records, which now put him alongside two of F1's greats.

items.title: Who slept worst last night: Fernando Alonso
items.summary: When Fernando Alonso became Formula 1 world champion in 2005, he was just 24 years old, replacing Emerson Fittipaldi as the youngest champion in the sport's history. At last, Michael Schumacher had a challenger.

items.title: Oscar Piastri splits from Mark Webber management
items.summary: Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have mutually agreed to terminate their management agreement, the pair have announced. Webber and his wife Ann – who ran Mark’s career herself back in the day – became Piastri’s managers in 2019, the year the youngster narrowly beat Victor Martins to the Formula Renault Eurocup title and a spot on Renault’s F1 academy.

items.title: Winners and losers from F1's chaotic Brazilian Grand Prix
items.summary: Are you not entertained? While Lando Norris took a well-deserved third win of the campaign, Mercedes collectively slipped up and Max Verstappen produced yet another Brazilian Grand Prix masterclass. Winner: Lando Norris McLaren team boss Andrea Stella loves describing Lando Norris as the low-grip master.

items.title: Max Verstappen gives emotional farewell gift to long-serving Red Bull mechanic
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has given his race helmet to long-serving Red Bull mechanic Ole Schack, who took part in his final race for the Milton Keynes outfit at Interlagos. Schack has been with Red Bull since its first season in 2005 and works on Verstappen's car as a front-end mechanic.

items.title: Charles Leclerc penalised for Liam Lawson clash; Kimi Antonelli and Oliver Bearman also punished after F1 Brazilian GP
items.summary: Charles Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix for his clash with Liam Lawson, dropping the Ferrari driver down to eighth place in the final results.

items.title: Max Verstappen "needs to understand what happened" after "night and day" F1 comeback in Brazilian GP
items.summary: For the third year in a row, Max Verstappen has produced an impressive comeback drive in Brazil. While he won from 17th on the grid in 2024 and drove from the pitlane to the podium last year, Verstappen finished this year's Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix in second place after starting 21st.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli: "Weird" spin and car instability cost F1 Brazilian GP win
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli vowed to put aside his Brazilian Grand Prix anger to celebrate Mercedes winning the Formula 1 constructors' title, as he rued the balance issues and the spin that took him out of victory contention. The new world champion had picked up the lead from polesitter Lando Norris at the start, and was building a pretty healthy lead over the Briton in the opening laps of the race.

items.title: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali sends heartfelt message to Mercedes after constructors' title victory
items.summary: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has congratulated Mercedes on winning the 2026 constructors' championship while singling out team principal Toto Wolff for joining Sir Frank Williams in the record books.

items.title: Lando Norris goes viral after Brazilian GP podium celebration goes wrong
items.summary: Lando Norris has gone viral on social media after his Brazilian Grand Prix podium mishap. The McLaren driver controlled almost everything that came his way at Interlagos, right up until he got to the podium.

items.title: Five quick takeaways from Brazilian GP
items.summary: Another impressive comeback drive from Verstappen, but Norris in a league of his own After qualifying, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton were in agreement: fighting their way through the field at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace would be considerably more difficult with the 2026 cars than in previous years.
